feed.title: Combined summary - [BIP draft] Unspendable Internal Keys for Wallet Policies

entry.title: Combined summary - [BIP draft] Unspendable Internal Keys for Wallet Policies
entry.summary: The recent discussions within the Bitcoin development community have led to a proposal concerning the standardization of an unspendable NUMS key specifically for script-path-only taproot policy. This initiative aligns with ongoing efforts to enhance security and functionality in Bitcoin scripting, without imposing strict adherence to other BIPs unless they are directly relevant. The primary aim is to normalize the use of unspendable keys within script descriptors to a certain extent without claiming semantic canonicalization. The approach involves defining a placeholder within the script to represent the unspendable NUMS key. Additionally, there is a methodological sorting of keys within `musig()` and `sortedmulti_a`, as well as sibling pairs in the tree structure. In scenarios involving multipath extensions, identical length tuples are added to ensure that key reuse does not occur. The entire structure, including the normalized descriptor and keys, is then hashed to generate a chain code according to BIP 341 standards. More detailed technical specifics can be accessed at [this link](https://github.com/bitryonix/bips/blob/bip-xxxx-unspendable-internal-keys/bip-xxxx-unspendable-internal-keys.mediawiki). A notable aspect of this proposed change highlighted by a peer review emphasizes its post-quantum security implications. Specifically, it enables provable non-spendability of script-path-only Taproot outputs. This feature is crucial for facilitating secure recovery processes where proving the non-spendability of a key path is necessary. Under the proposed system, the policy itself serves as evidence, allowing for the re-computation of the chain code and derivation of internal keys. This mechanism ensures that only those in possession of the original policy can produce requisite proofs, thus safeguarding against potential quantum computing threats that could compromise existing cryptographic checks. This enhancement has been suggested for inclusion in both the Motivation and Security sections of the BIP to underscore its significance beyond mere interoperability. These developments indicate a thoughtful progression towards securing Bitcoin's infrastructure against both current and emerging threats while maintaining a balance with operational practicality. They also reflect a broader dialogue among developers about how best to implement robust security measures in a decentralized digital environment.
